STAY_LOCAL: The stay is vertical at z 520, so the sim's global (x, y, z) force is the fairlead's local (pin, aft, up) force, as bag_attach / float_fea / loadpath_check use it.
H1 STL: stay tangent at z 520 within 5 deg of vertical (read off the print file before R1).
COMBINE: Worst rev C combination on one eye: the sim bag-hook vector and the rev C C5 IM3 meat-strap vector both at full value and added as vectors. This counts the meat weight twice (the sim hangs all of it on the bag, rev C puts 30 % of it and the overturning on the straps): an upper bound.
IM3 eye pull with both carabiners in the throat, the strap pulled aft and the hook pulled down at the same time (first frame).
LATERAL: The lateral (pin-axis) part of the hook pull bears on the inner face of one cheek, spread over the face within one hole diameter of the hole centre.
Same eye pull as COMBINE, with the hook 10 deg off the stay plane.
DIR_SCATTER: The combined hook + strap pull on the eye may sit up to 10 deg further aft than computed (the 18 sim hook vectors spread 2-8 deg aft; the strap angle at the eye is rev C's, not measured). The cheek must keep fatigue >= 1.15 at the computed angle + 10 deg.
IM3 eye pull test with the strap led aft at the measured hunting angle (first frame), or a protractor reading of the strap and hook angles in the T2 meat test.
PAHT_FAT: PAHT CF fatigue_1e5_ratio 0.30 (record ASSUMPTION, no published data).
CA-1 coupon test (TEST_PLAN): the flip points in section 5 say what each part needs.
SIM_BODY: Bag cases on the body: the sim's 1 g frame-side forces scaled by g x load / 68 kg; side-hill keeps the beam's lateral and downhill part, the upright part is replaced by the sim x cos 25 deg. The set is closed on the payload weight at the sim's CG: the force left over (under-straps, W straps, doublers and fabric the extraction does not map: 67-96 N, 10-14 % of the weight) goes to the four under-strap pins, and the sagittal moment left over to a fore-aft couple between the IM3 hook and hinge nodes (-38 to +201 N).
T9 loaded CG + frame strain gauges at the stays z 450-550 in the T1 carry test.
CINCH_STATIC: The meat straps' cinch (rev C 150 N per strap, the sim's meat-face push) is a static preload set at the kill site: it is in every strength and creep set but does not cycle with the walking g, so it is left out of the static-carry set that gives fatigue. The bound with the cinch cycling is reported beside it.
MT-1 strap tension readout over a 10 min loaded walk in the T2 meat test (amplitude of the strap tension against its mean).
SETDOWN_BEAM: The single-stay set-down keeps the beam's lumped bag masses (inertia relief through one foot); it does not enter fatigue.
STRAP_REACT: Meat case in the sim: the meat-face push is reacted at the six IM anchors: the overturning share per level and 30 % of the meat weight as in rev C, and the cinch loop (the spreader push it causes) by strap pulls at the three levels that balance that push in force AND moment (the meat bundle is in equilibrium), as near an equal split as that allows. The sim's push sits low (z 220-230), so the cinch goes almost all to IM1 (z 190).
MT-1 strap tension readout in the T2 meat test.

body_fix_md:
### 3.1 Smallest local fix tried: grow the stay sleeve's outer wall

Trials on the governing basis (fine sim, cinch static), smallest first: the outer radius of both stays' sleeves grown from 13.4 mm over a z band (spreader-clip sections and voids kept). Not an optimised shape: a first sizing for the print team.

| trial (z band, outer r) | added g per frame | fatigue 15 / 19 / 23 in | min fatigue | strength | creep |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| z 160-544, r 15.5 mm | 74.2 | 1.180 / 1.088 / 1.070 | 1.070 | 1.59 | 2.28 |
| z 160-544, r 17.5 mm | 191.2 | 1.246 / 1.149 / 1.131 | 1.131 | 1.69 | 2.41 |
| z 300-544, r 15.5 mm | 46.1 | 1.143 / 1.036 / 1.020 | 1.020 | 1.53 | 2.18 |
| z 400-544, r 15.5 mm | 18.2 | 1.128 / 1.022 / 1.011 | 1.011 | 1.51 | 2.16 |

**The 1.15 target cannot be reached by a small local fix.** Growing the sleeve wall outward barely moves the governing FI99 (it sits in the crown bore wall, where the carbon leg bears on the bushing seat, and is driven by the leg's couple, not by the stay's outer section): +18 g gives +0.010, the whole sleeve at +2 mm (+74 g) +0.069, +4 mm (+191 g) +0.130 and still 1.131. H1 passes rev C on the sim loads (fatigue 1.001 >= 1.0) but with no margin for scatter, and the result moves from 1.29 (coarse sim) to 1.00 (fine sim). What to do is in the report: settle the governing inputs (meat-case load split, cinch) with the T1 / T2 strain gauges before re-sizing the sleeve, and treat a bore-side change (longer or stiffer bushing seat, the 0.30 PAHT ratio from CA-1) as the design route, not wall mass.

fix_best.text: none of the sleeve-wall trials reached 1.15 (best 1.131 at +191.2 g); see 3.1.

body_method_md:
The H1 voxel body (frame_h1 solid, D's solver, FI99 rule, crown_diet.body_check) with the rev C bag cases (static carry, 2.5 g drop, side-hill torsion, hipbelt-off abuse) re-loaded from the cloth sim: per torso, the sim's frame-side forces at 1 g (both IM3 hooks as vectors at the z 520 stay nodes, both hinge pins at z 60, the guys at the crown top bar, the spreader / frame / crown contact node by node, under-straps and wraps at their anchors, the meat-face push reacted at the six IM anchors; ASSUMPTION STRAP_REACT), scaled by g x load / 68 kg (ASSUMPTION SIM_BODY). Whatever the sim does not put on a frame node (fabric self-weight, solver residual) goes to the four under-strap pins so each set carries the full bag weight. Fill and meat are separate scenarios (tags S_fill / S_meat); the non-bag rev C cases (set-down, meat straps, tall load, overload) are unchanged. Every torso is its own tag (BL-017's like-for-like basis). Fatigue and creep come from the static-carry sets (1.6 g / factor), strength from every set.

The beam basis (rev C weight split and the bag couple on the crown bar or on the IM3 hooks) is re-run on the same per-torso tags as the check of the method: it must reproduce BL-017's H1 per-torso body (fatigue 1.150).
